ledger-navy.$description: Ledger Navy — Hero bands, dark navigation, footer fields, and filled conversion controls — a dense blue-black base makes the electric interface panels appear illuminated

registry-blue.$description: Registry Blue — Product-console fields, logo marks, data-grid illumination, and active visual accents — vivid blue reads as a live system signal against Ledger Navy

network-teal.$description: Network Teal — Large feature-panel backgrounds and linked capability blocks — teal separates a data domain from the navy-and-blue product environment

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Page backgrounds, light header surfaces, cards, reversed type, logo rails, and hairline divisions

ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Editorial headlines, body copy, black feature panels, customer marks, and dark interface text

carbon.$description: Carbon — Near-black feature surfaces and dark data-card backgrounds

mint-paper.$description: Mint Paper — Pale alternate panels, metric-card surfaces, and subdued content blocks

sky-paper.$description: Sky Paper — Pale blue feature surfaces, interface outlines, and diagram highlights

rule-gray.$description: Rule Gray — 1px navigation separators, card divisions, and light-page rules

steel-rule.$description: Steel Rule — Cool 1px borders around light navigation controls and structured interface fields

quiet-gray.$description: Quiet Gray — Muted interface text and secondary navigation copy

season-vf.$description: Editorial display and section headings. The 515 variable weight avoids the hard authority of a bold headline; its near-touching 1.02 leading lets multi-line statements behave like a single typographic object.

uncut-sans.$description: Navigation, body copy, panel headings, cards, lists, and product-interface labels. Tight tracking at larger sans steps gives diagrams and capability panels a compressed technical cadence.

modern-era-mono.$description: Uppercase eyebrow labels, links, navigation utilities, status language, and button text. Mono labels make calls to action and field annotations feel like instructions from the verification system rather than promotional UI.
